owner_name: Sheffield United group (COH Sports, Steven Rosen and Helmy Eltoukhy)
note: Prince Abdullah bought Bramall Lane and other property back from Kevin McCabe's interests in 2020 after their court case, reuniting ground and club. COH Sports bought the club in December 2024 for about £105m including all real estate (Bramall Lane, Shirecliffe, hotel); the ground carries a mortgage to Emirates Bank per earlier reports.

lease_note: 99-year operating lease from 19 June 2012
note: The council built and owns the stadium; Doncaster Rovers took a 99-year operating lease in 2012 to run it. The Eco-Power naming deal ends after 2025-26, so the name may change.

After the 2011 administration Plymouth City Council bought the freehold for £1.6m and leased it back for 30 years. Under James Brent and then Simon Hallett the club bought the freehold back from the council for £2.7m (exact completion year not confirmed in the sources seen, after 2016).
sources: https://democracy.plymouth.gov.uk/documents/s48897/Home Park Football Stadium and Higher Home Park.pdf

owner_name: Wigan Council (land freehold); stadium leasehold held by a Mike Danson stadium company
lease_note: Stadium building held on long lease from the council; term not found
note: Wigan Council owns the freehold of the land. Owner Mike Danson has moved the stadium into its own company, separate from Wigan Athletic and Wigan Warriors, so the stadium interest would not pass automatically with the football club.

lease_note: Club holds a lease from the council; term not found
note: Cheltenham Borough Council owns the land and leases the ground to the club. In 2019 the council approved a land swap that changes the leased area on the terms of the existing lease.

lease_note: Club pays rent to the council; term not found
note: Wyre Borough Council owns Highbury and Fleetwood Town pay rent. The Pilley family rebuilt the stands after 2004 but did not take the freehold.

owner_name: Rochdale AFC (stadium company 100% owned by the club)
note: In 2016 Rochdale AFC bought out Rochdale council's and the Rugby League Facilities Trust's shares in the stadium company, giving the club 100% ownership; Rochdale Hornets are long-term tenants. The Ogden family bought the club in May 2024 and the ground stays inside the club group.

owner_name: County Ground Stadium Custodians Ltd (50% club/Clem Morfuni side, 50% TrustSTFC supporters' trust)
lease_note: 250-year lease back to the club from March 2023
note: On 24 March 2023 a joint venture of the club side and the supporters' trust bought the County Ground from Swindon Borough Council for £2.3m (funded by the Nigel Eady Trust) and leased it back to the club for 250 years. Reports differ on whether the non-trust half sits with the club or with owner Clem Morfuni personally; either way half is held by the trust, separate from the club.

lease_note: 30-year lease approved in 2018 at £25,000 a year before community-benefit discount (end year estimated from 2018 approval)
note: Meadow Park is a council-owned public park and the club leases the main ground and a second parcel from Hertsmere. The council approved a 25-year lease in 2013 and replaced it with a 30-year lease in 2018.

lease_note: Club operates/uses the ground under arrangement with the council; terms not found
note: Calderdale Council owns The Shay and decided in 2024 to stop running it. Its March 2025 decision to sell to Huddersfield Giants owner Ken Davy drew a legal challenge from Friends of The Shay, and Davy later withdrew, so the council still holds it and its future remains unsettled.

lease_note: 70-year lease from 19 June 1997
note: Hartlepool Borough Council owns Victoria Park and leases it to Hartlepool United Football Club Ltd. The council refused an earlier club offer to buy the stadium, and the club sought rent support during 2020-21.

owner_name: Unclear: a holding company owns the ground (Solihull Borough bought the site in 1999); its link to the current club owner was not established
note: Solihull Borough bought the former driving range in 1999 and built the ground; sources say a holding company owns it and tenants pay it rent. Solihull Council's Local Plan earmarks the site for Jaguar Land Rover expansion and the council can require the club to relocate, with a duty to help it move.

owner_name: Somerset Council (formerly South Somerset District Council)
lease_note: Leased back to the club owners from 17 May 2022; rent £229,130 a year after 2025 review; club holds option to buy back for £2.789m (indexed) until 17 May 2028
note: In 2022 South Somerset District Council bought the freehold of Huish Park and surrounding land for £2.8m in a sale-and-leaseback to keep the club afloat. Somerset Council has extended the club's buyback option from May 2026 to May 2028.

lease_note: Council approved a new 35-year lease (date and end year not confirmed); club had a 75% rent discount since 1977
note: Basildon Council owns the Blunts Wall Road site of New Lodge and leases it to the club. The newest source found on the lease is an undated older local news report (as_of year approximate), so terms may have changed since.

lease_note: Lease/licence terms not found
note: Chelmsford City moved in 2006 to the Melbourne Stadium, a council-owned athletics stadium (the former Chelmsford Sport and Athletics Centre).

owner_name: London Borough of Barking and Dagenham
lease_note: 30-year lease to March 2047
note: The council is the club's landlord at Victoria Road and granted a new 30-year lease running to March 2047 so the club could invest in the ground. Some guides wrongly say the club owns it.
sources: https://modgov.lbbd.gov.uk/Internet/documents/s27204/Dagenham and Redbridge Football Club Lease Report.pdf

ground: Cherrywood Road (sponsor names incl. Saunders Transport Community Stadium / Easy As HGV Stadium)
lease_note: 25-year lease extension agreed under owner Rob Prince (date not confirmed)
note: Researched Farnborough FC, the phoenix club formed after Farnborough Town folded in 2007, who play at Cherrywood Road. Rushmoor council owns the ground and granted the club a 25-year lease extension.

ground: Bowden Park (Harborough Town Community Football Ground)
note: Not established. Harborough District Council part-funded the 2018 3G pitch (including £270,000 of section 106 money) and a council document on leases with other organisations appears in searches for the ground, which suggests but does not prove council ownership.

lease_note: Long lease to 2070 confirmed 20 April 2024
note: Researched Hereford FC, the phoenix club formed in 2014 after Hereford United was wound up. Herefordshire Council owns Edgar Street and granted a lease to 2070, alongside plans to rebuild the Blackfriars End.

Maidenhead United own York Road, their home since 1871. The club bought land at Braywick Park from the Royal Borough of Windsor and Maidenhead in 2022 for a new stadium; after a 2023 refusal, the council began consultation in March 2026 on leasing up to 6.13 acres at Braywick to the club.

owner_name: Morecambe FC (majority owner Panjab Warriors since 2025)
note: The club built the Globe Arena in 2010 and put it in a separate company that later went into administration; on 19 August 2022 the club completed a land purchase with a balance owed to Ascot & Riley over five years, secured by a legal charge. Bond Group sold the club to Panjab Warriors in August 2025 after the club was briefly suspended by the National League.

owner_name: North Yorkshire Council (formerly Scarborough Borough Council)
lease_note: Club uses the council stadium; site run for the council by Everyone Active until management returns to the council in June 2027
note: Researched Scarborough Athletic, the phoenix of Scarborough FC (wound up 2007); the McCain Stadium is gone. Since 2017 they play at the council-owned Scarborough Sports Village.
sources: https://edemocracy.northyorks.gov.uk/documents/s53612/Replacement of the Community Football Pitch - Scarborough Sports Village.html?CT=2

owner_name: South Holland District Council as trustee of the Halley Stewart Playing Field Trust
lease_note: 25-year lease agreed with the trustee (start year not confirmed)
note: The field was gifted to the town in 1951 for community use and is held in a charitable trust whose sole trustee is South Holland District Council. Spalding United agreed a 25-year lease so they can access FA funding.

ground: Truro Sports Hub, Langarth (Truro City Stadium)
owner_name: Cornwall Council (via its development company Treveth)
lease_note: Short lease of the publicly owned hub, reported as being extended for a second year
note: Truro City lost Treyew Road when it was sold for a Lidl and played in exile at Plymouth Parkway. Cornwall Council's company Treveth built the Langarth sports hub and leases it to the club on short terms.

ground: Flamingo Park, Chislehurst (groundshare, 2026-27); previously Church Road
lease_note: Groundshare for the 2026-27 season
note: Church Road was bought by Irama Sports in 2021, which ended the old Whyteleafe FC's lease; phoenix AFC Whyteleafe then had a four-year deal there. After promotion to Step 3 they groundshare at Cray Wanderers' own Flamingo Park for 2026-27.

Researched Leamington FC, the re-formed successor of AP Leamington (the AP link ended in 1985). The club bought six acres on Harbury Lane from a local farmer for £30,000 and has played at the New Windmill since 2000; it also bought land at Europa Way in 2019 for a possible new ground.

The club bought derelict land in 1983 with help from South Ribble council and the Sports Council and opened Irongate in 1987, renamed after Sir Tom Finney in 2014. Local reporting says the club owns its ground and clubhouse; as an unincorporated club, title would be held by trustees for the members.

lease_note: Charitable lease to the company that runs the club; term not found
note: The freeholder BSGCA proposed in December 2020 to sell Broadwater for housing with developer Thakeham to fund a new sports hub at Bourne End (Bulbourne Cross); the club campaigned to stay and sought Asset of Community Value status. No final outcome was found; the club still plays at Broadwater in 2025-26.

lease_note: Lease from 2010; cabinet approved replacing it with a 50-year lease (completion not confirmed)
note: Researched Bromsgrove Sporting, who took the council's lease of the Victoria Ground in 2010 and gained sole use after Bromsgrove Rovers were expelled and dissolved that year. A council task group later recommended, and cabinet approved, a 50-year lease so the club can access grants.
sources: https://moderngovwebpublic.bromsgrove.gov.uk/documents/s43732/Cabinet Response to Bromsgrove Sporting Task Group.pdf

ground: War Memorial Sports Ground, Colston Avenue
lease_note: Lease from the council, varied to allow funding applications; term not found
note: Carshalton Athletic have played at Colston Avenue since 1920-21 and lease it from Sutton Council. The council agreed to vary the lease so the club could apply for funding, for example for a 3G pitch.

lease_note: Council ended the club's lease over health and safety and maintenance breaches but agreed the club can keep playing there; current basis of occupation not found
note: Chichester District Council owns Oaklands Park and has had long disputes with the club over a lease, including refusing one around 2011-12 and later ending the lease. The club still plays there; the date of the cancellation report was not confirmed.

lease_note: Terms not found
note: Tameside MBC built the £4m community stadium for Curzon Ashton, with a £500,000 Football Foundation grant, and the club moved in from National Park in 2005. Sources describe it as council-built; no lease details were found.

owner_name: Trustees of the Emley Moor Miners' Recreation Ground and Institute
note: Researched Emley AFC (AFC Emley 2005-2019), formed in 2005 after the old Emley AFC moved to Wakefield. The Welfare Ground is managed by the trustees of the miners' recreation ground charity, not by the club.

lease_note: Badgers Hill Ltd (Courtney Fong) holds a tenancy at will; planned long lease with option to buy not completed
note: Frome Town Council bought Badgers Hill from Frome Town Holdings Ltd in 2022 and first leased it to a community benefit society. In July 2025 it agreed a lease with option to buy to Badgers Hill Ltd, removed that exclusivity in December 2025, and in April 2026 rejected both bids for lack of proof of funds, leaving the ground's future unsettled.
Not established. Guiseley have played at Nethermoor since 1909 and have submitted phased ground development plans to Leeds City Council, but no source seen states who holds the freehold.

Not established. Westleigh Park was acquired by Havant Town in 1980 and opened in 1982; the merged club has played there since 1998, but no source seen says whether the club, the council or another party holds the freehold now.

owner_name: Private landowner (not named in sources seen)
lease_note: 25-year lease of ground and clubhouse, replacing earlier one-year deals (start year not confirmed)
note: Kettering Town left Rockingham Road and, after spells elsewhere, moved in at Latimer Park with Burton Park Wanderers. The club agreed a 25-year lease with the site's landowner; Burton Park Wanderers and a boxing club keep using the site.
